newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end quiet session moderately weaker.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end quiet session moderately weaker.

text.p: NYCE Frozen concentrated orange juice ended weaker Monday after spending most of the session in negative territory, as uncertainty about the size of Florida's orange juice crop kept many traders away from the market, trading sources said.
November FCOJ closed 1.60 cent a lb lower at 104.85, having traded from 104.60 to 106.50. The back months also lost ground, easing 1.00 to 1.20 cent per lb.
Volume on the day was estimated at 1,100 lots, up from 302 lots in the previous session.
Traders said many operators appeared hesistant to take positions ahead of the U.S. Department of Agriculture's upcoming estimate of Florida's 1996/97 crop. The USDA forecast is due out on October 11.
"There's really a lack of interest in the market," said one analyst. "The outlook is really dependent on the report, and the trade can't do much until it is issued."

Following today's losses, most-active November appeared poised to test support at around 104.00 cents. November's contract low of 103 cents hit in early September could also be challenged, chartists said.
